CLAUSE 4 IS UNMEASURABLE AND IS REPORTED AS AN ABSENCE RATHER THAN PASSED. game/data/quests/hooks.json declares deadlines as the empty array. QuestMachine.onDay(dayCount) at sim/quest/machine.js:712 is the only deadline consumer in the tree, and grep over game/ and tools/ returns EXACTLY ONE occurrence of onDay - its own definition. Nothing in the running world calls it: a correct model with no caller, which is the RI-MTH07 shape this project has shipped sixteen times. Driven by hand it does reach fail(), so the model is right and the wiring is missing. The quest-layer clock reader that DOES work is the journal date stamp: four rests take it from 1 Second Seed to 2 Second Seed, 3E 427.

THE AR-1 DEFECT ROUND 3 SHIPPED, AND THE CONTROL THAT FINDS IT IS SAME-FRAMES-ALIVE, NOT DELETE-THE-FIX. Round 3 held the world clock while a death is in flight (correct, RI-PRG04 section 6 rule 4) and sim/souls.js reads that same field for the 21:00-05:00 night multiplier. So the frames a player spends dead cost them no night time. MEASURED on the round-3 tree: from 04:30, forty deaths leave one ordinary enemy paying 57 where the same 6,040 frames spent ALIVE leave it paying 42. Dying paid 35 per cent more. Symmetrically at 20:58 dying pays 42 and living pays 57. Round 3 compared shipped against the round-2 clock and never against a living player, which is why nobody saw it.

THE FIX: sim/environment.js section 1b - env.awardTimeOfDay, a second clock that ticks whether the player is alive or dead and is RE-SEATED on the world clock whenever anything outside the step writes it (a rest, setTimeOfDay, a load). _syncFromFloat already detected exactly that event, so the discharge is three lines and the death-stolen offset cannot accumulate across the hearth loop - which is the loop this item is about. sim/souls.js awardFor() reads it. ONE LINE of another piece file, declared redundant_with W1-SOULS-r3.

SHIPPED AFTER THE FIX: 04:30 dying 42 = alive 42; 20:58 dying 57 = alive 57. The invariant holds in BOTH directions. AWARD CLOCK DELETED: 04:30 dying 57 vs alive 42; 20:58 dying 42 vs alive 57. THE ARMS DIFFER - RULES.md 6, written and run.

AND THE DEADLINE BURN WAS NOT GIVEN BACK. Forty deaths burn 0.003703 h of WORLD clock on the shipped tree - forty frames, one per death, which is round 3s already-characterised residual against a ceiling of 0.003796 - against 0.559259 h with round 3s clock hold deleted. 151x. The world clock is still held; only the rate the souls economy reads has been detached from it.

NEXT-DISPATCH section P.6: THE LEVEL SPEND IS NOT REACHABLE BY INPUT ALONE, and it is measured rather than read off the source (reports/runs/W1-13-R4/input-only.json). I DID NOT LAND THE UI FIX. Named with its acceptance instead of landed. Section P.5 stays met; section P.6 needs this branch and then a recorded session.

TWO INERTNESS GUARDS CAUGHT MY OWN PROBE TWICE, AND BOTH EARLIER ANSWERS WERE THE RIGHT ANSWER FOR THE WRONG REASON. Draft 1 passed absolute frame numbers to queueInputs (HARNESS.md section 4 says they are RELATIVE to the call frame) and opened nothing at all - caught by a guard requiring the probe to open at least one screen. Draft 2 opened the inventory but every press inside it was swallowed - caught by a getUIState fingerprint control, because mode cannot tell a swallowed press from a no-op. Draft 3 uses round 3s own recipe (f:0, one frame per edge) and roll, menu and both horizontal axes demonstrably move the screen. The first two verdicts are recorded as void.
